original_question: Fix d in N and epsilon in (0,1). What is the least k = k(d,epsilon) such that every degree-d polynomial threshold event over a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X approximates the corresponding event under a standard Gaussian vector Z within additive error epsilon; that is, |Pr[p(X) >= 0] - Pr[p(Z) >= 0]| <= epsilon for every degree-d polynomial p : R^n -> R?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the open problem titled "k-wise Independence for PTFs," whose official statement asks for the least k=k(d,ε) so that k-wise independent standard-Gaussian marginals fool every degree-d polynomial threshold event. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it fixes d∈N and ε∈(0,1), asks for the least k=k(d,ε), quantifies over every degree-d polynomial p:ℝ^n→ℝ, compares the probabilities of the threshold event {p≥0} under X and under a standard Gaussian vector Z, and uses k-wise independent Gaussian coordinates as the pseudorandom model. This matches the structure and intent of the paper's statement almost verbatim. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
missing_details: The paper quantifies over every ambient dimension n, so a fully stand-alone version should say explicitly: for every n∈N. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
It should specify that X is an arbitrary ℝ^n-valued random vector X=(X1,…,Xn), not just a vaguely described distributional object. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))

The marginals are required to be standard Gaussian individually: each Xi has the standard Gaussian distribution N(0,1), not merely some unspecified Gaussian marginal. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
The meaning of k-wise independence should be spelled out exactly as in the paper: every subcollection Xi1,…,Xik is independent. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
Z should be defined explicitly as the standard n-dimensional Gaussian vector, i.e. Z∼N(0,In). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))

The official formulation is specifically about the zero-threshold event {p(x)≥0}; it should not be broadened to arbitrary thresholds or a more general class of threshold predicates. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))

The paper says "degree-d multivariate polynomial" over ℝ and imposes no homogeneity, multilinearity, normalization, bounded-coefficient, or other structural restriction on p; a faithful stand-alone rewrite should preserve the absence of those extra assumptions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))

Because this paper is a short list of open problems and explicitly defers notation/definitions to standard references, the rewritten question should carry its own notation rather than relying on external conventions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
refined_question: Fix d∈N and ε∈(0,1). Determine the least integer k=k(d,ε) such that the following holds: for every n∈N, every degree-d multivariate polynomial p:ℝ^n→ℝ, and every ℝ^n-valued random vector X=(X1,…,Xn) with the properties that each Xi has the standard Gaussian distribution and every k-tuple Xi1,…,Xik is independent, one has |Pr[p(X)≥0]−Pr[p(Z)≥0]|≤ε, where Z∼N(0,In) is the standard n-dimensional Gaussian. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
justification: arXiv:1204.6447 is not a theorem-driven paper with items like Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it is a compiled list of open problems. In that list, the exact nearest target is the problem headed "k-wise Independence for PTFs" on page 9, and your draft already tracks its statement closely. The nearby remarks then give the known bounds for d=1, d=2, and general d, which confirms that the intended question is precisely to optimize the dependence of k on d and ε for fooling degree-d polynomial threshold events under k-wise independent standard Gaussians. The rewrite therefore keeps the problem narrow and paper-faithful while only making explicit the ambient dimension quantifier, the exact meaning of k-wise independence, and the standard-Gaussian assumptions on X and Z. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))
